title: Enemy AI is compiled Lua 5.0 shipped with each map
summary: Every enemy thinks with compiled Lua 5.0 scripts: shared chunks in aicommon.luabnd plus a per-map copy of each enemy's logic and battle goal. NpcThinkParam names the pair by logicId and battleGoalID.
values: aicommon.luabnd has 104 chunks (ai_define, goal_list, table_ai_common ...). Soldier row 10100000: logicId 101000, battleGoalID 101000 (files 101000_logic.lua, 101000_battle.lua). NpcThinkParam: 771 rows, 154 distinct battleGoalID; most used logicId 101000 (91 rows), 150000 (48), 155000 (45).
how: The exe embeds the Lua VM and registers about 230 AI methods (IsBattleState, AddSubGoal, GetExcelParam ...). Scripts run the goal tree; native goal classes do the movement and attacks.
check: Load m11_00 luabnd, run 101000_battle with a Wolf stand-in, and read the goal start/end log (tests ai_stubs, duel_trace).
note: Both ports run the unchanged bytecode. Ours dropped the decompiler step on 2026-10-09 and uses Lua 5.0 bytecode directly.

title: Goal kinds: table goals, script goals, native goals
summary: A goal is a table goal (REGISTER_GOAL, Goal.Activate/Update/Terminate/Interrupt), a script goal (<Name>_Activate ...) or a native engine class (Wait, Stay, MoveToSomewhere, Guard, SidewayMove, KeepDist, LeaveTarget, SpinStep, Parry, CommonAttack ...). Subgoals run front first; a failed subgoal fails its parent.
values: CommonAttack 2200 has empty script callbacks, so it is the native class. TimingSetNumber/TimingSetTimer defer a SetNumber/SetTimer to AI_TIMING_SET__ACTIVATE (0) or UPDATE_SUCCESS (1).
how: AddSubGoal/AddTopGoal build the queue; the engine updates the front subgoal, then the goal's own update. Interrupts offer events to the logic first, then goals from deepest up.
check: Run a soldier fight and read the goal log: approach, CommonAttack, ComboFinal appear as nested goals.
note: Update order and lifetime rules are ours in sekiro-rs (marked 'ours' in AI.md); RustSekiro traced the native classes in the exe.

title: A goal whose life runs out fails unless SetLifeEndSuccess
summary: When a goal's life reaches 0 while its update still says Continue it counts as Success only if it or a goal above it has SetLifeEndSuccess; otherwise it Fails, the parent fails and the queued subgoals are dropped.
values: Exe: FUN_1405faa20 sets goal +0x4a0 bit 0x20; FUN_1405d06c0 and FUN_1405d1b50 (walk up) decide. Wait/Stay/Guard end by life as a success (updates not traced).
how: Fixes the old assumption that every timed out goal succeeds: a timed out approach no longer lets the queued CommonAttack swing from out of reach.
check: Sim test a_timed_out_goal_fails_unless_life_end_success; in game watch an enemy whose approach times out: it replans instead of swinging.
note: sekiro-rs rule: Wait/Stay/Guard/Sideway succeed at end of life, everything else fails. RustSekiro's rule is the exe one.

title: Logic.Main picks the goal; battle goals roll weighted acts
summary: When the top goal's queue is empty or Replanning was called, the engine runs the think row's logic. COMMON_EzSetup first handles alert-state transitions, then _COMMON_SetBattleActLogic chooses between a reply to help, a battle goal, the caution/find goals or a non-battle goal.
values: Battle goals fill a 1..N odds table (defAct01..defActNN) from distance, target guard, SpEffects and cool-downs; Common_Battle_Activate rolls the table with the engine's random numbers (GetRandam_Int) and the chosen Act queues approach plus attack subgoals. Soldier example: distance >= 7 and target guarding gives acts 3 and 5 weights 100 and 200.
how: Table goals: Goal.Activate scores acts, Goal.Update is Update_Default_NoSubGoal, so the battle goal ends when its subgoals do and the logic runs again.
check: Dump the goal log for a soldier at 8 m vs a guarding Wolf and count the acts picked over 60 s; act 5 and 3 dominate.
note: RNG is a seeded xorshift in ours and sekiro-rs, so act choices match in distribution only.

needs.why: the logic reads the target state

title: Target state: NONE, CAUTION, FIND, BATTLE
summary: Each enemy keeps one target state derived from its target slots: a normal target is FIND and then BATTLE, while sound, corpse, indication position and last-memory targets give CAUTION; nothing gives NONE. The previous state is kept so scripts can detect a change.
values: Names AI_TARGET_STATE__NONE 0 / CAUTION 1 / FIND 2 / BATTLE 3. Target types: NORMAL_ENEMY 3, SOUND 4, MEMORY_ENEMY 5, INDICATION_POS 6, CORPSE_POS 7. AI SpEffects: 200000 normal, 200001 non-combat caution, 200002 combat caution, 200004 find/battle. State at SprjTargetingSystem (AiThink +0x7b30), field +0x158, previous +0x15c.
how: FUN_14061ff40 updates the slots; FUN_1406208c0 derives the state in priority order (normal, then sound 4, corpse 7, indication 6, memory 5 give CAUTION). A change replans unless the row's goalAction_ToCaution/ToFind is 0.

his.where: crates/sim/src/lua_ai/runtime.rs (visible target -> FIND next run -> BATTLE; no sound/indication/memory slots)

check: Walk into a soldier's cone in a sim: trace shows NONE -> FIND -> BATTLE and AI SpEffect 200004; throw a firecracker out of view for CAUTION.
note: sekiro-rs fakes the state from visibility. RustSekiro ports the targeting system from the exe.

title: Sight: the normal cone (eye_*_normal)
summary: A soldier sees Wolf inside a cone: from eye_BeginDist to eye_dist away from an eye point pushed eye_BackOffsetDist behind its feet, inside left/right and upper/bottom angles. Seeing Wolf in this cone makes him a normal target (FIND).
values: Soldier row 10100000: eye_dist 20 m, begin 4, back offset 4, yaw +-30 deg, pitch +10 up / -15 down, so about 16 m ahead of the body. General 10200000: yaw +-45, up 15. Shichimen 10800000: 50 m. Owl 50600000 / Isshin 54000000: dist 120, begin 80, back 80, yaw +-15, up 4, down 15 (about 0..40 m ahead). Headless 13500000 and Female Musician 70000000: yaw 180 pitch 90 (all around). 169 rows use 25 m, 150 use 20 m, 48 rows 120 m.
how: Test FUN_14061bb70: eye = feet - facing*back*cut; begin*cut <= d < radius + dist*cut; yaw in [-left, right]; pitch in [-bottom, upper]; then a line-of-sight ray. Light factor 1 / 0.5 / 0.3 scales it. Target point is Wolf's feet, radius is his capsule radius.
check: In a sim place a soldier facing +Z and Wolf at 15 m, 25 deg off axis: seen. At 17 m or 35 deg: not seen. Tests in src/sim_tests/part04.rs.
note: Wolf's capsule radius is taken as 0.4 (not traced). The exe check uses Wolf's feet point.

title: Sight: the wide 'around' cone fills an alert meter
summary: Outside the normal cone but inside a wider, shorter-range 'around' cone, a detection meter fills at aroundTargetIncrementPoint per second. At 100 the enemy gets an indication target at Wolf's spot and turns to CAUTION; the meter drains 20 per second outside the cone.
values: Soldier row 10100000: around dist 40 m, yaw +-30, +25 points/s so 4.0 s to fill (trace: full at 4.0 s). 491 rows use 25/s, 239 rows 0 (no around sense: bosses, Shichimen), 9 rows 1000 (instant, row 50101050-54), 11 rows 40. Indication target forgotten after IndicationTargetForgetTime (150 s for most). Wolf's stealth SpEffects 3391/3441/150000 multiply the fill by aroundSightPointAddRate 0.5.
how: FUN_140625340 adds IncrementPoint * dt * product(aroundSightPointAddRate); FUN_140612400 drains 20/s out of the cone; FUN_140626430 turns >= 100 into an IndicationPos slot (FUN_1406285c0).
check: Stand in a soldier's around cone for 4 s without entering the normal cone: it turns to caution and walks to your spot.
note: HUD stealth bar is drawn over the enemy (hud.rs); art is a stand-in.

title: Sight: the 'perceive' set keeps a found target
summary: Once an enemy is in FIND or BATTLE its normal-cone test switches to the larger 'perceive' set (flag 0x100000), so a found Wolf is held at a longer range than the range that first spotted him.
values: Soldier row 10100000: perceive dist 40 m (normal 20), yaw +-30. The set uses the same offset/begin fields with _perceive suffix.
how: FUN_14061bb70 picks the perceive set when the target state flag is set.
check: Get found at 15 m, then back off to 30 m in the open: the soldier keeps tracking until SightTargetForgetTime runs out out of sight.

title: Sight search runs every 0.2-0.4 s and needs a clear line
summary: The sight test is not run every frame: each enemy searches at a random 0.2-0.4 s interval. The final step is a collision ray between the enemy and Wolf; a hit means not seen. The meter update runs every frame.
values: Interval = rand*0.2 + 0.2 s (DAT_143afb488 / 48c). Ray: FUN_14061c8a0, filter 0x32, through FUN_14094e310. Detection time at the cone edge is about 0.5 s at eye_BeginDist and up to 3 s at eye_dist (kb damage.md, not traced).
how: FUN_140623ca0 schedules the search; the normal cone casts the ray unless ctx +0xc2 is set.

ours.where: src/stealth.rs sight_clear (both points taken as capsule centres)

check: Stand behind a thin wall inside a soldier's cone: not seen. Step out and count frames until FIND (0.2-0.4 s granularity).
note: Which collision filter bits 0x32 skip is unknown; ours raycasts the hit collision only.

title: Dark and pitch-dark collision halves vision
summary: Each map collision part has a visibility (Good, Dark, Total Dark). The sight query scales distances by 1 / 0.5 / 0.3, remapped by Wolf's mapVisibilityOverride* SpEffect fields. NpcThinkParam disableDark = 1 skips it (20 rows).
values: Factors DAT_143afb490..8 = 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.3. Collision type data +0x27: 0 Good, 1 Dark, 2 Total Dark. All 221 collision parts of m11_01 are Good. Dark ones: m11_00 has 2 Dark + 4 Total, m17 19 Total, m20 7. disableDark rows include 10100330, Headless 13400000.
how: FUN_1409b5c80 writes the part's visibility into chr +0x1acd; FUN_140617150 puts it in the sight query; FUN_14061ae40 / FUN_14061c2a0 scale by query +0x58[type].

ours.where: src/stealth.rs (light level fixed at Good: map visibility not exported)

check: Stand in a Dark-visibility cave on m11_00: soldier sight reach halves (20 m to 10 m).
note: Visibility bytes are not exported by our map tools. 109201 may be driven by this (open question).

title: FIND turns into BATTLE inside BattleStartDist
summary: A found Wolf only starts a fight when he comes within BattleStartDist; farther away the enemy stays in FIND (alert, approaching). A hit on the enemy (reason 4) puts it in BATTLE at once.
values: Soldier 12 m (215 rows), General 15 m, Shichimen 50 m. Common values: 12 m (215), 25 m (78), 30 m (72), 20 (67), 50 (57), 15 (44), 45 (33), 9999 (23 rows: always battle once found). The distance is dimmed by darkness unless disableDark.
how: FUN_14062be40 FIND -> BATTLE; damage path FUN_14061d140. A platoon battle also forces it.
check: Get spotted at 18 m by a soldier: it plays the find reaction and closes in; at 12 m the fight starts. Hit it first: instant fight.
note: Paramdex's Description for BattleStartDist is a copy of callHelp_MyPeerId (labelling slip), not trusted.

title: How long enemies remember Wolf
summary: Each target slot has its own forget time. The sight target is forgotten after SightTargetForgetTime while unseen, sound after SoundTargetForgetTime, memory after MemoryTargetForgetTime, indication position after IndicationTargetForgetTime, a corpse after CorpseTargetForgetTime.
values: Sight: 15 s (317 rows incl. soldiers 10100000), 10 s (126), 99999 (95 bosses/never), 3600 (69, General), 3 s (49). Memory: 150 s default (542 rows), 5 s (53), 9 s (48), 99999 (75). Sound: 150 (555), 99999 (74), 9 (48), 5 (29). Indication: 150. Corpse: 150. Soldier-like: 15 s sight, 150 s memory.
how: SightTargetForgetTime counts down while the normal target is unseen; reaching 0 clears the normal target and leaves the last-seen position as a memory target (CAUTION).

ours.where: src/stealth.rs: forget runs on the normal target; LastSightPos bookkeeping missing

check: Break line of sight to a soldier at 10 m and hide: it searches ~15 s and then walks home (trace SHINOBI_STEALTH_TRACE=lose).
note: Memory vs sight handover is only partly modelled in ours.

title: Hearing: AI sounds with a radius, a rank and a listener range
summary: Noises are AI sounds (AiSoundParam rows with radius, rank, life and who can hear). A listener hears a sound when it is closer than hearing-rate times radius less ear_soundcut_dist, plus its ear_dist.
values: reach = rate * radius - ear_soundcut_dist; heard while dist - radii < reach + ear_dist. rate = product(1 - hearingSearchEnemyCut/100) of the listener's SpEffects (FUN_140bfe590); sound rows flagged bSpEffectEnable also scale by the owner's hearingSearchEnemyRate. ear_dist: 0.1 m on 633 rows, 0 on 117, 6 m on 16 dog-type rows (c1150), 18/25/30 on four. Rows per AiSoundParam: 90.
how: SprjAiSoundNormalListener, FUN_140610470 (flags selfTarget / opposeTarget / friendlyTarget), range FUN_140610a30 / b30; manager FUN_14064a5f0.
check: A soldier with ear_dist 0.1 hears a walking Wolf (radius 0.5) only inside about 0.6 m, a running Wolf (2) inside 2.1 m; dogs add 6 m.
note: Deaf SpEffects: hearingSearchEnemyCut 100 on firecracker, 200110 and 200140; test a_deafened_enemy_hears_nothing.

title: Wolf's footsteps, sprint and landing noises
summary: Wolf's movement clips carry CreateAISound (TAE 237) and make a sound whose radius depends on how he moves: crouched is quietest, sprint and swimming the loudest.
values: Radius per AiSoundParam id (all rank 0): walk 1000 = 0.5 m, crouch walk 1001 = 0.25, crouch run 1011 = 0.5, run 1010 = 2 m, sprint 1020 = 4 m (SprintStartFromStep 1151, SprintLoop 1200, quick turn), cover/hang moves 1002/1003 = 0.25, jump start 1300 = 2, wall jump 1320 = 0.5, landing from a free fall 1310 = 2 (0.03 s event on the 'start from free fall' clips), step from damage 1100 = 4, grapple shot 1200 = 2, swim moves 1014/1015 = 2, swim kick 1024/1025 = 4, deflect 2030 = 8 (rank 1). Life 0.25 s for the 1000-1015 rows, 1 s for 1100+.
how: TAE 237 on c0000 anims (70 distinct anims with 1310, 54 with 1300, 35 with 1010 ...). Walk/run sound events last the whole clip (2.77 s walk, 1.77 s run).

ours.where: src/enemy.rs wolf_sounds (read from the clip on screen)

check: Sneak up behind a soldier: walking crouched (0.25 m) is silent, running (2 m) is heard from 2 m, sprinting from 4 m.
note: Sound id names (walk, sprint, landing) were matched through statemap_c0000.json animId to state name; the AiSoundParam rows have no names.

title: Combat noise: Wolf's swings and hits are sounds too
summary: Wolf's attacks announce themselves: each AtkParam_Pc has an AppearAiSoundId (when the attack is issued) and a HitAiSoundId (on each target hit, guarded or not). They are rank 1 'important' sounds with wider radii than footsteps.
values: Appear ids: 2010 (224 rows, radius 2), 2000 (44, 1), 2020 (37, 4), 2150 (8, 12), 2140 (4, 6). Hit ids: 2110 (223, 4 m), 2100 (42, 2), 2120 (26, 8), 2130 (16 m), 3500. Deflect 2030 (8 m). Exe emits Appear once per attack at the attacker (FUN_1409a1290) and Hit once per target (FUN_1409e68e0).
how: SprjAiSound entries live for AiSoundParam lifeFrame. rank 1 raises goalAction_ToCautionImportant instead of goalAction_ToCaution.
check: Swing near an unaware soldier behind a corner at 2 m: it notices. Heavy hit sounds reach 4 to 16 m.
note: Hit emitter owner is inferred as the attacker.

title: Normal vs important sounds change the caution reaction
summary: A sound has rank 0 (normal) or 1 (important). Hearing an important sound runs the row's goalAction_ToCautionImportant instead of goalAction_ToCaution, and a few sound ids tune the approach distance.
values: Rank 1 rows: Wolf deflect 2030, combat sounds, ape/ally calls 4000-4100 (30-200 m, friends only), 5000-5400 (4-20 m), 7400 rank 3. Special ids in the logic: 7900 and 7910 stop the approach at 0.4 m, 3501 at 0.2 m, 7700 forces a confirm-caution look.
how: _COMMON_AddCautionAndFindGoal picks the action by GetLatestSoundTargetRank() == AI_SOUND_RANK__IMPORTANT.

ours.where: src/ai.rs (rank answered; per-row actions via GetExcelParam)

check: Compare the reaction to a thrown firecracker (important) vs a walk: the first approaches, the second only looks.

title: Alert spreads through friendly call sounds on attacks
summary: When an enemy attacks, its attack emits a 'call friend' AI sound. Friends in the same placement group who hear it join the fight, so one alert pulls in the group. It only works while the caller is in BATTLE or FIND.
values: NPC attack rows: AtkParam_Npc AppearAiSoundId 2000025 (1243 rows, 10 m) and HitAiSoundId 2000020 (1223 rows, 20 m); flags bCallFriend + bRestrictSamePlacementGroup + friendlyTarget, rank 1, life 0.1 s. Other call sounds: 2000000 (20 m, the spot-call), 2000010 (30), 2000100 (20), 2103000 (10), 2111000 (50), 2112000 and 2122000 (60), 2155000 (30). Rows 4020-4100 are friendly-only sounds.
how: SprjAiSound with friendlyTarget heard by same-group listeners; the heard sound becomes a rank-1 sound target, then the row's goalAction_ToCautionImportant runs.
check: Alert one soldier in a camp, hit him once: the others within 10 to 20 m with the same group turn to your position.
note: Whether the group test uses MSB placement group or an AI group id is not traced.

title: NpcThinkParam call-for-help fields are unused
summary: The TeamCallHelp / TeamReplyHelp goals exist in the Lua, but callHelp_MyPeerId, callHelp_CallPeerId and callHelp_CallValidRange are 0 on all 771 rows. In the shipped data no enemy shouts for help through that path.
values: All 771 rows: callHelp_* = 0. platoonReplyTime = (1.0, 2.0) on 734 rows. The scripts common_team_call_help.lua / common_team_reply_help.lua are reachable only when peer ids are non-zero.

check: Dump NpcThinkParam callHelp_*: all zero. No sim needed.

title: Platoons: shared state and formation
summary: Some groups act as a platoon with a leader script. The platoon has its own state (None 0, Caution 1, Find 2, ReplyHelp 3, Battle 4), a formation, and a catch-up speed so members keep together. Orders reach members as PlatoonAiOrder interrupts.
values: common_000100_platoon.lua: formation, catch-up move rate 0.7 to 1.5, distances 5 and 10, command distance 5. maps/000120_platoon.lua is the map copy. AI_INTERRUPT_PlatoonAiOrder = 42.
how: Platoon goals run on a leader object; members get AI orders through the interrupt and act in their battle goal.
check: Find a platoon group in m11_00 (MSB platoon refs) and watch members hold formation while one patrols.
note: Which enemies belong to platoons has not been listed (open question).

title: Attack, surround and spectate roles
summary: When several enemies fight, a manager hands out roles every 0.1 s: attackers, surrounders (Torimaki) and spectators (Kankyaku). Only attackers go in, so crowds do not all strike at once.
values: ROLE_TYPE Attack 0, Torimaki 1, Kankyaku 2, None -1. Counts 1 attacker and 1 surrounder (tunables DAT_143afb990 / 994 / 998). TeamAttackEffectivity per row: 34 (323 rows), 0 (134), 100 (74). A weighted mode (DAT_143afb99c) is off. The 101000 and 102000 battle scripts read the role and use thinkAttr_doAdmirer to hang back.
how: FUN_140640b80 calls FUN_140640050 every 0.1 s over the group.
check: Face 3 soldiers: one attacks and one circles at a time; the third stands back.
note: Weighted mode never exercised; the role order inside a group is by distance (not traced).

summary: On CAUTION the enemy runs ConfirmCautionTarget: it goes to the sound or last-seen spot, looks left and right, waits 3 to 8 s and, if nothing turns up, returns to non-battle behaviour.

values: Default notice clip 1040. Notice clip lengths vary by chr. The reaction is skipped when the row's goalAction is 0.

title: goalAction_* columns pick the reaction style
summary: Six NpcThinkParam columns pick how an enemy reacts to each state change: to caution, to important caution, to find, to a corpse, to an indication position and to disappear. Values are small ints from 0 to 5.
values: Common combos (ToCaution, ToCautionImportant, ToFind, ToCorpse, ToIndication, ToDisappear): (2,3,3,3,2,2) 148 rows, (2,2,2,2,2,2) 110, (1,1,1,1,1,1) 98, (0,0,0,0,0,0) 55. Meaning: 0 default turn then ConfirmCautionTarget; 1 turn and stay or look; 2 approach (path check, run); 3 approach with forced-walk region; 4 stay and look; 5 keep away 2.5 m.
how: _COMMON_AddCautionAndFindGoal reads the column for the current trigger.

title: Leash: enemies give up and walk home
summary: An enemy fights only while Wolf is near its post. If Wolf leaves the leash range the enemy stops and returns to its home point. Closer to home the leash is looser: it fights inside backhomeBattleDist and goes home otherwise.
values: Soldier row 10100000: backhomeDist 48 m (563 rows; 115 rows have 9999 = no leash), maxBackhomeDist 64 m, backhomeBattleDist 8 m, BackHomeLife_OnHitEneWal 6 s. Rule in _COMMON_SetBattleActLogic: if target is searchable and maxBackhomeDist < movePointEffectRange go home; else if backhomeDist < range fight only when distance < backhomeBattleDist; else fight.
how: Distance measured from the enemy's home (spawn) point to Wolf. NonBattleAct BackToHome follows.
check: Run 50 m from a soldier's post: it quits and turns home, then patrols again.

title: Enemies deflect on a timer by rank A, B or C
summary: Enemies decide to guard or deflect Wolf's attack by a rank set on the enemy: A deflects a thrust always, B half the time, C never. The check runs every 0.1 s and needs Wolf inside the front cone.
values: Rank SpEffects: 221000 rank A (201 NpcParam rows: General 10200000/10203010, Genichiro 71001000, Isshin 54000000, Owl 50600000), 221001 rank B (374), 221002 rank C (605: Ochimusha 10100000). Common_Parry (common_common_func_NTC.lua:333): Wolf in 90 degree front cone and AI in Wolf's 90 degree cone within GetDist_Parry. Wolf thrust 109970: A 100 % deflect (3101), B 50 %, C 0. Wolf unguardable 109980 and rank A: spin step 5201/5211. Otherwise deflect 3101 with chance ConsecutiveGuardCount*50, else guard 3100. Wolf rush 109990 forces EndureAttack guard (off if self 220062 or Wolf 110450/110500/110501).
how: Timer AI_TIMER_PARRY_INTERVAL 0.1 s; InterruptParryTiming 24 hands the decision to Common_Parry.

title: Consecutive-guard counter raises deflect chance
summary: An enemy remembers how many of Wolf's attacks it guarded in a row. Each guard adds 1 and the deflect chance is that count times 50 percent, so a second guard in a row deflects. It resets after 1 s.
values: SpEffects 200215 / 200216 add 1 (reset after 1 s by timer 13); 200210 / 200211 reset it; 200250 weak-guard counter.
how: Read by Common_Parry (see ai.parry-rank).

title: Guard stance and 'AI is guarding' state
summary: Enemies hold a guard stance by action id. 9910 is the guard action; 9920 is the general stance. A guarding enemy blocks front hits and spends posture; scripts check it to choose acts.

Wolf's own recoveries: 110015, 106065/6. UseItem goal exists but only changes the equip item.

title: AI interrupts: events the logic can react to
summary: Besides replanning on timers, the engine offers named interrupts to the goals: Damaged, FindAttack, ParryTiming, Inside_ObserveArea, SpEffect on/off and platoon orders. Scripts return true to take them.
values: INTERUPT_FindAttack 1, Damaged 2, Inside_ObserveArea 16, ParryTiming 24, PlatoonAiOrder 42, ActivateSpecialEffect 43, InactivateSpecialEffect 44, UseItem. Interrupts go to the logic first, then the goals from the deepest one up.
how: Engine queues the interrupt; AddObserveSpecialEffectAttribute registers a SpEffect watch.
check: Hit an enemy mid-approach: the Damaged interrupt cancels its goal and replans.

title: SpEffect watch fires only for the named character
summary: AddObserveSpecialEffectAttribute fires only when the character named in the call gets or loses the SpEffect. Matching on any character fires scripts too often.
values: Fix in ours: AiState::observes checks the owner.
how: Interrupts 43 and 44 carry the owner.
check: Sim test: give an unrelated chr the watched SpEffect: the enemy does not react.

title: Turning on the spot uses 90 or 180 degree clips
